turns.user: My son just called me crying, said he's been in an accident and needs ₹50,000 transferred right now to a hospital account, he sounded scared and hung up quickly. I don't know what to do.
replies: It sounds incredibly frightening to get a call like that from your son, especially when he sounded so distressed and needed money urgently for a hospital. This is a common type of impersonation scam designed to make you act quickly without thinking. First, we need to make sure your son is safe. There are five things to do here: 1. Call only official numbers (card, app, website) 2. Report it on Chakshu (sancharsaathi.gov.in) 3. Warn family about impersonation calls 4. Agree a family secret word 5. Explain how this scam works

Let's start with the most urgent step: please try to reach your son directly on his usual number or through someone else in the family, not by replying to the message or call you just received. This will help you verify if he is truly in an emergency. Please let me know once you've tried this.

replies: That's a huge relief to hear your son is safe and well.

Scammers can now use AI to fake a familiar voice, or even a face on a video call. So even if it sounds or looks like someone you know, that alone is not proof it is really them, that is exactly what makes this trick work. If you'd like me to take you through it step by step, just reply yes.

turns.user: Yes, please guide me step by step.
replies: Okay, let's report this call on Chakshu. Here's how to do it:

1. Go to the Sanchar Saathi website: sancharsaathi.gov.in 2. On the homepage, click on the "Chakshu" option. 3. Fill out the form with the details of the call you received, including the phone number it came from and a brief description of what happened. Please let me know once you've done this, or if you get stuck at any point.

turns.user: OK, I will report it on the Chakshu portal now.
replies: Thanks for letting me know you'll report it on Chakshu. Please tell me once you've completed it, or if you have any trouble with the website.

replies: Well done for reporting it on Chakshu.

The next important step is to warn your family members, especially those who might be vulnerable, that someone might try to impersonate you or another relative. Tell them that if they get an urgent call asking for money, they should always call back on a number they already know is correct for that person, and not just reply to the message or call they just received. If you'd like me to take you through it step by step, just reply yes.

replies: That's good that you're going to verify with family. Now, let's set up a secret word with your family.

Choose a word that only your close family members know. If anyone calls asking for urgent money, you can ask them for this secret word. If they don't know it, you'll know it's not really your family member.

Now, it's important to tell your whole family exactly how this call worked, so they can spot a similar scam before any money is sent.

turns.user: I got a call saying a parcel booked in my name was caught at Mumbai customs with drugs and a fake passport inside. He said he’s transferring the call to the Cyber Crime branch. Now a “police officer” is saying I need to share my Aadhaar number and bank details to prove my innocence or my account will be frozen
replies: If the call is still on, hang up now. You do not have to stay on it.

It sounds like a really frightening call about a parcel and drugs, and it's good you're checking before sharing any details. The police or any official agency will never ask you for your Aadhaar number or bank details over the phone to prove your innocence or threaten to freeze your account. This is a common tactic in digital arrest scams.
